ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three rectangular prisms made from two identical rectangular-prism bricks. The upper middle figure is two bricks stacked one above the other, marked with surface area 72; the lower left figure is two bricks placed side by side horizontally, marked with surface area 96; the right-side figure is two bricks joined end to end along the length direction, marked with surface area 102. These three ways of assembling correspond to the two identical bricks being respectively attached on three different types of faces. Reasoning: Let the surface area of one brick be P, and let the areas of the three different faces of the brick be A, B, and C, then P = 2(A+B+C). If the two bricks do not touch, the total surface area is 2P; when they are attached along a face of area A, what is hidden is two such faces on the two bricks, so the surface area after being assembled is 2P - 2A. Similarly, when attached along the other two types of faces, the surface areas are respectively 2P - 2B and 2P - 2C. The three ways of assembling in the figure exactly correspond to three different attached faces, so 72 + 96 + 102 = (2P-2A) + (2P-2B) + (2P-2C) = 6P - 2(A+B+C). Because P = 2(A+B+C), so 2(A+B+C)=P, therefore the sum is 6P - P = 5P. Thus 5P = 72 + 96 + 102 = 270, P = 270/5 = 54.
